sources.entry: quokka - Inspect and clean a USB-connected iPhone from the macOS terminal: storage, apps, media, syslog. No jailbreak.

summary.one_liner: quokka is a Mac command-line tool (also installed as the short alias qk) that inspects and cleans a USB-connected iPhone or Android phone from the terminal, without jailbreak or root.
summary.what_it_does: It shows device status, identity, and battery, and lists installed user apps by size with uninstall support. It surveys and analyzes media files (camera roll and downloads), can flag likely duplicates, and can delete files through an interactive picker. It streams the device system log (syslog or logcat) in a TUI viewer with level and process filters, search, pause, and save, or as plain text. It can also reboot or power off the device, and renders a 1080x1080 PNG device snapshot card. Every query command supports --json output, and --redact masks serial, UDID, IMEI, and MAC.
use_cases: Free up storage on a test iPhone or Android phone
Find the largest apps and uninstall them from the terminal
Tail a device's system log while debugging
Find duplicate photos and videos on a connected phone
Pull device info for scripts or CI with JSON output
Make a shareable device info screenshot with masked identifiers
notable: Works on iPhones over usbmuxd and lockdown services without jailbreak or core_device_proxy tunnel
Supports both iOS 17+ and Android 8+ over adb, with no root on either
Plain-text and NDJSON streaming modes for piping into jq or CI
Redaction applied before JSON serialization for safe sharing
Separate presentation-free core crate intended for a GUI to build on
caveats: Requires a USB cable, a trusted device, and Xcode command line tools for iPhone; adb and USB debugging for Android
On Android without root, app names show as package ids, battery health and cycles are unavailable, and qk capture is iOS-only
Some features (interactive pickers, deletion) need a TTY
